items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: he didn't get behind Willard Alexander, the booking agents, to keep us busy

ctx.x: conscientious about it. Because Rudy Palmer, my lead alto, was very important to me then, teaching the other saxophone players the way to make a tone for section work, (inaudible) because he had studied this with a fine teacher and he got Ben -- they didn't play the same when they took their solos as when they played in the section, to get the blend of the horns. So my band was working on those sort of values. I'm very proud of, and oh, it was really a bitter pill when it had to go. We just couldn't keep our…

Then, too, John Hammond, he didn't believe in it. He could have kept us going but he didn't get behind Willard Alexander, the booking agents, to keep us busy. So they just used us like a football, selling us cheap and telling us they couldn't get no money for us. I couldn't hold the band together, the payrolls, you know. (Inaudible).

But he had all those big guys and let me just throw some of these names at you that we can kind of talk about. There's Keg Johnson, which was your friend and my friend. He was in "Tailspin", he was with Benny Carter. And did you do much for Tommy Dorsey? Jack Teagarden --
